title: Pictures Hidden in Stars
question: What are constellations, and how do people use them?
hook: The stars in a pattern are usually not neighbours at all.
idea: Constellations are imagined figures drawn from star patterns, and the stars in them usually lie at very different distances.

beats.prompt: Tens or hundreds of thousands of years from now, you look at a familiar constellation. What will you see?

choices.label: The same outline as today
choices.feedback: It seems the sky never changes, but each star has its own independent motion.

choices.label: An outline that has become unrecognizable
The same outline, but dimmer
choices.feedback: Brightness is not the issue; the stars themselves move relative to one another.

beats.explain: Each star has its own independent motion, so after tens to hundreds of thousands of years familiar outlines will become unrecognizable.

items: Astrological zodiac divisions become prominent in Babylonian or Chaldean astronomy
Constellations of the far southern sky begin to be added
The IAU accepts the modern list of 88 constellations
The IAU adopts official constellation boundaries
beats.explain: The zodiac divisions date to about 400 BC, southern constellations came from the 15th century, and the IAU acted in 1922 and then 1928.

beats.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: Never sets below the horizon from a given latitude
A star pattern that is not a formal constellation
A number plus the constellation's genitive name
beats.explain: Each term describes a different way that stars are grouped or named in the sky.
The Big Dipper sits within Ursa Major and the teapot within Sagittarius; the patterns are asterisms and the larger areas are constellations.
